title: Eighth Word The Unfortunate Brothers Suspicion And Painful State

questions.question: Where did the man end up after traveling over rough land?
questions.answer: In a lonely wild place.

questions.question: What scared the man first in the wilderness?
questions.answer: A huge lion.

questions.question: Where did he jump when he got very afraid?
questions.answer: Into a dry well.

questions.question: How did he stop himself from falling all the way down?
questions.answer: He grabbed a tree growing from the wall.

questions.question: What were the two animals doing to the tree?
questions.answer: They were chewing its roots.

questions.question: What did the man see above him at the top of the well?
questions.answer: The lion waiting there.

questions.question: What did he see below him?
questions.answer: A scary dragon.

questions.question: What else was around him on the sides of the well?
questions.answer: Harmful stinging bugs and creatures.

questions.question: What was strange about the fig tree?
questions.answer: It had many kinds of fruit on it.

questions.question: Why did the man fail to understand what was happening?
questions.answer: He was foolish and did not think carefully.

questions.question: Did he understand that a mighty ruler was controlling these things, or did he think it was all ordinary?
questions.answer: He thought it was all ordinary.

questions.question: What were his heart and mind doing deep inside?
questions.answer: They were full of pain and sorrow.

questions.question: What did his selfish side pretend?
questions.answer: That everything was fine.

questions.question: What did he start doing with the fruit?
questions.answer: He began eating it.

questions.question: Why was eating some of the fruit a bad idea?
questions.answer: Some of it was poisonous and hurtful.

questions.question: What does the sacred saying teach about how a servant thinks of Allah?
questions.answer: A person is dealt with according to how he thinks of Allah.

questions.question: What happened to the man because of his wrong thinking?
questions.answer: He stayed in suffering and could not escape it.

questions.question: Did he find peace by dying or by truly living?
questions.answer: Neither; he remained in torment.

questions.question: What problem met the man in the lonely land?
questions.answer: A dangerous lion came after him.

questions.question: What did fear make him do next?
questions.answer: It made him jump into a dry well.

questions.question: Why did he not fall straight to the bottom?
questions.answer: His hands caught a tree.

questions.question: What danger was coming from the tree itself?
questions.answer: Two rats were cutting through its roots.

questions.question: What color were the two rats?
questions.answer: One was white and one was black.

questions.question: What danger was above the well, and what danger was below?
questions.answer: The lion was above, and the dragon was below.

questions.question: What made the walls of the well dangerous too?
questions.answer: Poisonous stinging creatures were there.

questions.question: What surprising thing did the man notice about the tree’s fruit?
questions.answer: One tree had many different kinds.

questions.question: What important truth did the man miss about the strange scene?
questions.answer: He missed that it was not random and had hidden meaning.

questions.question: Who was really in control, even though the man did not understand it?
questions.answer: A powerful one was in control.

questions.question: What was happening inside his heart, spirit, and mind?
questions.answer: They were crying in grief.

questions.question: What did his nafs do instead of listening to that inner pain?
questions.answer: It ignored the warning and fooled him.

questions.question: What shows that the man acted carelessly?
questions.answer: He ate the fruit as if he were safe in a garden.

questions.question: What does the hadith in this passage say in a simple way?
questions.answer: How we think of Allah matters.

questions.question: How did the man think about what he saw?
questions.answer: He thought it was just normal life.

questions.question: What was the result of that wrong view?
questions.answer: He was left in misery.

questions.question: Why is his condition especially sad?
questions.answer: He cannot get out of his pain.

questions.question: At the end of the passage, why is the story about him paused?
questions.answer: So attention can turn to the other brother.

questions.question: What came out of the forest and threatened the man?
questions.answer: A lion.

questions.question: What kind of well did he jump into?
questions.answer: A deep well without water.

questions.question: What helped him hang in the middle of the well?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the side.

questions.question: What were the white and black rats doing?
questions.answer: They were biting the roots.

questions.question: Why was the man trapped?
questions.answer: Danger was above, below, and around him.

questions.question: Name one danger above the man and one below him.
questions.answer: The lion was above him, and the dragon was below him.

questions.question: What made the tree unusual?
questions.answer: It carried many kinds of fruit.

questions.question: Did the man see these events as signs with a secret, or as ordinary things?
questions.answer: As ordinary things.

questions.question: What does that tell us about the man’s thinking?
questions.answer: He was not thinking wisely.

questions.question: How were his inner feelings different from what his nafs acted like?
questions.answer: Inside he was hurting, but his nafs acted like nothing was wrong.

questions.question: What wrong choice did his nafs push him to make?
questions.answer: To eat the fruit carelessly.

questions.question: Why was that choice unsafe?
questions.answer: Some fruit was harmful.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the sacred hadith placed in the passage?
questions.answer: A person’s thoughts about Allah affect how he is treated.

questions.question: What kind of thoughts did this man have about what Allah was doing?
questions.answer: Low and mistaken thoughts.

questions.question: What happened because he judged the whole scene the wrong way?
questions.answer: He remained in deep suffering.

questions.question: What two things did not happen for him: rescue through death or comfort through life?
questions.answer: He did not die, and he did not truly live in peace.

questions.question: What feeling best describes his state at the end of this part: joy, comfort, or torment?
questions.answer: Torment.

questions.question: After running through the wilderness, what danger made the man flee?
questions.answer: A fierce lion.

questions.question: What did he use for support inside the well?
questions.answer: A tree.

questions.question: What shows that the tree could not hold forever?
questions.answer: Its roots were being eaten by two rats.

questions.question: How did the dragon make the danger even worse?
questions.answer: It lifted its head close to him.

questions.question: Besides the lion and dragon, what other creatures threatened him?
questions.answer: Poisonous stinging creatures.

questions.question: What would make someone wonder about the fig tree right away?
questions.answer: It had many different fruits on one tree.

questions.question: Why should the man have realized this was not an ordinary scene?
questions.answer: The things there were too strange to be random.

questions.question: What big idea did he fail to understand about the strange beings around him?
questions.answer: They were under the control of a powerful ruler.

questions.question: What were his heart and spirit doing even though he ignored them?
questions.answer: They were crying out in pain.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the evil-commanding nafs?
questions.answer: It can hide the truth and trick a person.

questions.question: How did the nafs trick him in this story?
questions.answer: It made him act as if he were in a pleasant garden.

questions.question: What poor action followed that trick?
questions.answer: He ate fruit that was not all safe.

questions.question: Why is the hadith about thinking of Allah important here?
questions.answer: It explains why his bad outlook led to bad treatment.

questions.question: What kind of outlook did the man have?
questions.answer: A foolish and mistaken one.

questions.question: What happened to him again and again because of that outlook?
questions.answer: He stayed in suffering.

questions.question: Why is his pain described as ongoing?
questions.answer: He is not freed from it.

questions.question: What does the narrator do after describing his misery?
questions.answer: Leaves him there and turns away.

questions.question: Why does the narrator turn away from him?
questions.answer: To look at the other brother’s case.

questions.question: What was the first frightening creature in this passage?
questions.answer: A lion.

questions.question: What did the man do because of fear?
questions.answer: He jumped into a deep dry well.

questions.question: What stopped him halfway down?
questions.answer: A tree caught in the wall.

questions.question: What two small animals were harming the tree?
questions.answer: A white rat and a black rat.

questions.question: What huge creature waited below?
questions.answer: A dragon.

questions.question: What other danger filled the sides of the well?
questions.answer: Poisonous little creatures.

questions.question: What made the tree seem amazing?
questions.answer: It grew many kinds of fruit.

questions.question: Did the man think deeply about these signs?
questions.answer: No, he did not.

questions.question: What should he have understood about all these unusual things?
questions.answer: That they were not there by accident.

questions.question: Who did he fail to recognize behind these events?
questions.answer: A mighty one directing them.

questions.question: What was his heart doing while he acted careless?
questions.answer: It was grieving.

questions.question: Which part of him acted proudly and wrongly?
questions.answer: His nafs.

questions.question: What did his nafs choose instead of listening to the warnings inside him?
questions.answer: It chose to enjoy the fruit.

questions.question: Why was that enjoyment false?
questions.answer: Some fruit brought harm.

questions.question: In this passage, what does thinking wrongly about Allah lead to?
questions.answer: It leads to being treated in a painful way.

questions.question: What was wrong with how the man saw his situation?
questions.answer: He took a serious warning as something normal.

questions.question: What is the sad result of his mistake?
questions.answer: He remains in misery without relief.

questions.question: Where was the man when he heard a terrible sound?
questions.answer: In a lonely wilderness.

questions.question: What animal appeared and made him run?
questions.answer: A lion.

questions.question: Into what place did he throw himself?
questions.answer: A deep dry well.

questions.question: What did he grab inside the well?
questions.answer: A tree.

questions.question: What were the two rats doing to that tree?
questions.answer: They were chewing through the roots.

questions.question: What did the man see when he looked up?
questions.answer: The lion still waiting above.

questions.question: What did he see when he looked down?
questions.answer: A dragon near his feet.

questions.question: What did he notice on the walls of the well?
questions.answer: Dangerous stinging creatures.

questions.question: What was special about the fig tree near him?
questions.answer: It had lots of different fruits.

questions.question: Why did the man misunderstand the whole event?
questions.answer: He lacked wisdom and careful thought.

questions.question: What hidden truth did he miss?
questions.answer: That there were secrets and a ruler behind it all.

questions.question: Even though he was in trouble, what did his nafs pretend?
questions.answer: That it was no big problem.

questions.question: What did his nafs keep him from hearing?
questions.answer: The cries of his heart and spirit.

questions.question: What did he do as if he were safe and comfortable?
questions.answer: He ate from the tree.

questions.question: Why was that dangerous?
questions.answer: Some of the fruit was poisonous.

questions.question: What simple lesson is taught by the sacred hadith in this part?
questions.answer: We should have good thoughts about Allah.

questions.question: How did this man think about what was happening to him?
questions.answer: He understood it in a wrong and shallow way.

questions.question: What final condition was he left in?
questions.answer: Pain and torment without escape.
